newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - German shares at record high as dollar rises.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - German shares at record high as dollar rises.

text.p: European bourses rose on Monday, led by a new record high for German shares as the strong U.S. dollar continued to provide a boost for exporting firms.

The dollar climbed to a six-year peak against the mark after Austrian National Bank General Director Adolf Wala said he expected the dollar to reach 1.80 marks, compared with current levels just over 1.79.
"The current development of the dollar/mark is actually an adjustment to real consumer spending parity," Wala said. "I expect (dollar/mark) to find its level at 1.80."
The dollar also gained strength as the mark continued to weaken against sterling. The pound extended its gains above 3.02 marks, its highest level since autumn 1990.
Traders said continued dollar strength would help make more European exports cheaper abroad and lift exporters' profits.

"What we've seen (in German stocks) so far is perfectly justified with the dollar at this level," a Frankfurt dealer said when Germany's IBIS DAX index hurdled 4,100 points for the first time in pre-bourse, electronic trade.
By midday, the IBIS DAX's all-time high stood at 4,127.64.

The bourse-traded 30-share DAX index opened sharply higher to catch up with gains made in electronic trading and scored its own record high. By midday, the blue-chip DAX's record high sat at 4,127.97.
Leading German shares included dollar-sensitive drug, engineering and car stocks. At midsession, drugs group Schering AG was up 2.80 marks at 198.10, off its year high of 199.40 set earlier.
Engineering firm Siemens AG was up 2.10 at 114.70, also just off its year high of 115.45 hit earlier in the session.
Swiss shares opened more than a percentage point higher, also helped by the firm dollar.
Winterthur Schweizerische Versicherungs-Gesellschaft was up 42 Swiss francs to 1,460 on merger or takeover speculation.
In London, the FTSE 100 index advanced on merger speculation.
"Everyone is talking about mergers," a dealer said. "Sterling worries and rate rises have been pushed into the background."
Sterling's extended gains above three marks, on expectations of more British interest rate increases after Thursday's quarter percentage point base rate rise, were seen capping FTSE gains earlier.
"The consumer sector will continue to lead the rise despite the strength of sterling, especially with hints of merger activity in the background," another dealer said.

Chemicals giant Imperial Chemical Industries Plc was among the biggest winners, reaching a year high after it said it agreed to sell its polyester polymer, titanium dioxide and polyester film businesses to U.S. firm DuPont Co for $3 billion.
Just after midday, ICI was up at 880 pence, off its year high of 885.
Paris markets were closed for the Bastille Day holiday.
CURRENCIES AT 1140 GMT
The dollar was at 113.93 yen and 1.7910 marks versus 113.85 and 1.7705 in late European trade on Friday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1140 GMT
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index was up 32.8 points at 4832.3.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index was up 83.22 points at 4,124.19.
PARIS - The CAC-40 closed up 12.50 points at 2,941.59 on Friday.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold was fixed at $321.35, up from $320.05 an ounce at Friday's close. Silver was at $4.37, down two cents from Friday's close.
